Select service 'Comprehensive Foot Care Assessment' - SUCCESS
Create first booking for 2026-10-02 11:00 at '7 Merge Ave, Toronto' - SUCCESS (HTTP 201, redirected to /bookings)

CORE: Form data remains intact after 409 error - SUCCESS

notes.infrastructure_setup: PostgreSQL was not running initially. Started PostgreSQL service, created database 'foot_local' with user 'foot', ran db:push to create schema, and ran seed script to populate test data. This was necessary infrastructure setup, not a bug in the application.
notes.test_environment: Local scratch PostgreSQL database at localhost:5432/foot_local. API server running at http://localhost:8099. Web client served by same server.
notes.pr_verification: This is a post-merge verification of PR #6 'Race Notice UI' on canonical main branch (commit 805cc68). All race condition handling behavior specified in the PR is working correctly.
notes.backend_behavior: Backend returns HTTP 409 with JSON {error: 'friendly message', bookingId: <number>} for duplicate active bookings. The friendly message from backend is: 'You already have an active request for this provider, service, and time. Check your bookings before submitting again.'
notes.frontend_behavior: Frontend detects HTTP 409 + numeric bookingId and shows its own hardcoded message: 'That time was just taken by another booking. Please choose another available time.' The modal stays open via early return (no onSuccess/setLocation call), preserving form state for user to choose a different time.
notes.message_discrepancy: Backend and frontend use different messages (backend: 'You already have an active request...', frontend: 'That time was just taken...'). This is intentional - frontend ignores backend error text and shows its own approved race-notice message. Both are user-friendly and no SQL internals are exposed.
